reason: R2 only provides a DC reference/leak path for the net44 node, which is otherwise mainly used as the other terminal of C0. If you remove R2, net44 becomes floating (unless something else biases it), but the core differential amplifier signal path (VIN1 → VOUT1) is largely unchanged.
impact_estimate: Low–Medium: OK for basic functionality, but can cause an unreferenced/floating node and convergence issues in SPICE; add a large-value bleed resistor if needed.

reason: C0 appears to be a compensation/AC-shaping capacitor between VOUT1 and an auxiliary node (net44), not essential for establishing the amplifier’s DC operating point. Removing it typically leaves DC gain/biasing intact, but changes frequency response and stability margins.
impact_estimate: Low for DC operation; Medium–High for transient/AC stability (possible ringing/oscillation depending on loading and biasing).

reason: R3 is most likely a load/bleeder providing a defined DC path at the output; many amplifier cores still bias and operate without it if another load exists. If your testbench or next stage already loads VOUT1, R3 can be removed with little functional change.
impact_estimate: Low if VOUT1 has another DC load/path; Medium if VOUT1 would otherwise float (output common-mode may drift and simulations may have convergence issues).
